p203.zh: 假设巴西货币(实值)的市场汇率为35美分/实值,每天市场交易额为150亿,如(a)和(b)中的E0平衡所示。 然而,巴西政府决定,汇率应为30美分/实际汇率,正如(a)所示。 也许巴西将这一较低的汇率用于出口行业。 也许这是通过刺激出口刺激总需求的一种尝试。 也许巴西认为,目前的市场汇率高于真实物的长期购买力平价,因此,巴西通过保持这一较低的汇率,将真实物的波动降到最低。 或许政府过去某时设定了目标汇率, 无论出于何种原因,如果巴西中央银行希望将汇率维持在市场水平以下,就必须面对这样的现实,即按照30美分/实际的这一较弱汇率,其170亿里亚尔的货币需求量将大于外汇市场130亿里亚尔的供给量。

p205.original: The Brazilian central bank could weaken its exchange rate in two ways. One approach is to use an expansionary monetary policy that leads to lower interest rates. In foreign exchange markets, the lower interest rates will reduce demand and increase supply of the real and lead to depreciation. Central banks do not use this technique often because lowering interest rates to weaken the currency may be in conflict with the country’s monetary policy goals. Alternatively, Brazil’s central bank could trade directly in the foreign exchange market. The central bank can expand the money supply by creating reals, use the reals to purchase foreign currencies, and avoid selling any of its own currency. In this way, it can fill the gap between quantity demanded and quantity supplied of its currency.
p205.zh: 巴西中央银行可能会以两种方式削弱其汇率。一种办法是采用导致利率下降的扩张性货币政策。 在外汇市场上,较低的利率将减少对实体的需求和增加供应,并导致贬值。中央银行不经常使用这种技术,因为降低利率以削弱货币可能与国家的货币政策目标相冲突。 或者,巴西中央银行可以在外汇市场上直接交易。中央银行可以通过创造真币,利用真币购买外币来扩大货币供给,避免出售任何自己的货币. 这样,它就能填补所需数量与所供应货币数量之间的差距。

p206.original: (b) shows the opposite situation. Here, the Brazilian government desires a stronger exchange rate of 40 cents/real than the market rate of 35 cents/real. Perhaps Brazil desires the stronger currency to reduce aggregate demand and to fight inflation, or perhaps Brazil believes that that current market exchange rate is temporarily lower than the long-term rate. Whatever the reason, at the higher desired exchange rate, the quantity supplied of 16 billion reals exceeds the quantity demanded of 14 billion reals.
p206.zh: (b) 显示相反的情况。 巴西政府希望比35美分/实际的市场汇率更强劲。 也许巴西希望更强的货币来减少总需求并遏制通货膨胀,或者也许巴西认为目前的市场汇率暂时低于长期汇率. 无论出于何种原因,按照更高的预期汇率,所供应的160亿实体数量超过了要求的140亿实体数量。

p207.original: Brazil’s central bank can use a contractionary monetary policy to raise interest rates, which will increase demand and reduce currency supply on foreign exchange markets, and lead to an appreciation. Alternatively, Brazil’s central bank can trade directly in the foreign exchange market. In this case, with an excess supply of its own currency in foreign exchange markets, the central bank must use reserves of foreign currency, like U.S. dollars, to demand its own currency and thus cause an appreciation of its exchange rate.
p207.zh: 巴西中央银行可以使用收缩的货币政策来提高利率,这将增加外汇市场的需求和减少货币供应,并导致升值。 或者,巴西中央银行可以直接在外汇市场进行交易。 在这种情况下,由于外汇市场上自身货币供应过剩,中央银行必须使用外汇储备,如美国美元,来要求使用自己的货币,从而导致其汇率升值.

p208.original: Both a soft peg and a hard peg policy require that the central bank intervene in the foreign exchange market. However, a hard peg policy attempts to preserve a fixed exchange rate at all times. A soft peg policy typically allows the exchange rate to move up and down by relatively small amounts in the short run of several months or a year, and to move by larger amounts over time, but seeks to avoid extreme short-term fluctuations.
p208.zh: 软挂钩和硬挂钩政策都要求中央银行干预外汇市场。 然而,硬挂钩政策始终试图保持固定汇率。软挂钩政策通常允许汇率在短短几个月或一年中以相对小的金额上下移动,并随着时间推移以较大金额移动,但力求避免极端的短期波动.

p209.original: Tradeoffs of Soft Pegs and Hard Pegs
p209.zh: 软便便便和硬便便便的权衡

p210.original: When a country decides to alter the market exchange rate, it faces a number of tradeoffs. If it uses monetary policy to alter the exchange rate, it then cannot at the same time use monetary policy to address issues of inflation or recession. If it uses direct purchases and sales of foreign currencies in exchange rates, then it must face the issue of how it will handle its reserves of foreign currency. Finally, a pegged exchange rate can even create additional movements of the exchange rate. For example, even the possibility of government intervention in exchange rate markets will lead to rumors about whether and when the government will intervene, and dealers in the foreign exchange market will react to those rumors. Let’s consider these issues in turn.
p210.zh: 当一个国家决定改变市场汇率时,它面临着一些权衡。 如果它使用货币政策来改变汇率,那么它就不能同时使用货币政策来解决通货膨胀或衰退的问题. 如果它使用汇率直接购买和销售外币,那么它就必须面对如何处理其外币储备的问题。 最后,挂钩的汇率甚至会造成汇率的进一步变动。 例如,即使是政府干预汇率市场的可能性,也会引发关于政府是否以及何时干预的谣言,外汇市场的经销商也会对这些谣言作出反应. 让我们反过来考虑这些问题。

p211.original: One concern with pegged exchange rate policies is that they imply a country’s monetary policy is no longer focused on controlling inflation or shortening recessions, but now must also take the exchange rate into account. For example, when a country pegs its exchange rate, it will sometimes face economic situations where it would like to have an expansionary monetary policy to fight recession—but it cannot do so because that policy would depreciate its exchange rate and break its hard peg. With a soft peg exchange rate policy, the central bank can sometimes ignore the exchange rate and focus on domestic inflation or recession—but in other cases the central bank may ignore inflation or recession and instead focus on its soft peg exchange rate. With a hard peg policy, domestic monetary policy is effectively no longer determined by domestic inflation or unemployment, but only by what monetary policy is needed to keep the exchange rate at the hard peg.
p211.zh: 对挂钩的汇率政策的一个关切是,它意味着一国的货币政策不再注重控制通货膨胀或缩短衰退,而现在还必须考虑到汇率。 例如,当一个国家将其汇率挂钩时,它有时会面临经济情况,它希望有扩张性的货币政策来对付衰退,但它不能这样做,因为这一政策会降低其汇率,打破其硬挂钩。 由于汇率政策松软,中央银行有时可以忽略汇率,而注重国内通货膨胀或衰退,但在其他情况下,中央银行可能忽视通货膨胀或衰退,而侧重于其软挂钩汇率。 由于实行硬挂钩政策,国内货币政策实际上不再由国内通货膨胀或失业决定,而只能由维持硬挂钩汇率所需的货币政策决定。

p212.original: Another issue arises when a central bank intervenes directly in the exchange rate market. If a central bank ends up in a situation where it is perpetually creating and selling its own currency on foreign exchange markets, it will be buying the currency of other countries, like U.S. dollars or euros, to hold as reserves. Holding large reserves of other currencies has an opportunity cost, and central banks will not wish to boost such reserves without limit.
p212.zh: 另一个问题是,中央银行直接干预汇率市场。 如果一个中央银行最终陷入在外汇市场上不断创造和出售自己货币的局面,它将购买其他国家货币,如美国美元或欧元,作为储备。持有大量其他货币的储备具有机会成本,中央银行不会希望不加限制地增加这种储备。

p213.original: In addition, a central bank that causes a large increase in the supply of money is also risking an inflationary surge in aggregate demand. Conversely, when a central bank wishes to buy its own currency, it can do so by using its reserves of international currency like the U.S. dollar or the euro. However, if the central bank runs out of such reserves, it can no longer use this method to strengthen its currency. Thus, buying foreign currencies in exchange rate markets can be expensive and inflationary, while selling foreign currencies can work only until a central bank runs out of reserves.
p213.zh: 此外,一个造成货币供应大幅增加的中央银行也有可能出现通货膨胀猛增的总需求。 相反,当中央银行希望购买自己的货币时,它可以通过使用其国际货币储备,如美元或欧元来购买。 但是,如果中央银行没有这种储备,它就不能再使用这种方法来加强其货币。 因此,在汇率市场购买外国货币可能代价高昂,而且会出现通货膨胀,而出售外国货币只有在中央银行储备用尽时才能起作用。

p214.original: Yet another issue is that when a government pegs its exchange rate, it may unintentionally create another reason for additional fluctuation. With a soft peg policy, foreign exchange dealers and international investors react to every rumor about how or when the central bank is likely to intervene to influence the exchange rate, and as they react to rumors the exchange rate will shift up and down. Thus, even though the goal of a soft peg policy is to reduce short-term fluctuations of the exchange rate, the existence of the policy—when anticipated in the foreign exchange market—may sometimes increase short-term fluctuations as international investors try to anticipate how and when the central bank will act. The following Clear It Up feature discusses the effects of international capital flows—capital that flows across national boundaries as either portfolio investment or direct investment.
p214.zh: 还有一个问题是,当政府将其汇率挂钩时,它可能会无意中造成另一个引起额外波动的原因。外汇交易商和国际投资者通过软挂钩政策,对中央银行如何或何时干预影响汇率的谣言作出反应,当他们对谣言作出反应时,汇率就会上下转移。 因此,即使软挂钩政策的目标是减少汇率的短期波动,但当外汇市场预期的政策存在时,随着国际投资者试图预测中央银行将如何和何时采取行动,短期波动有时会增加。 以下的Clearing Up专题讨论了国际资本流动的影响——资本作为证券投资或直接投资跨越国界流动。

p215.original: How do Tobin taxes control the flow of capital?
p215.zh: 托宾税如何控制资本流动?.

p216.original: Some countries like Chile and Malaysia have sought to reduce movements in exchange rates by limiting international financial capital inflows and outflows. The government can enact this policy either through targeted taxes or by regulations.
p216.zh: 智利和马来西亚等一些国家试图通过限制国际金融资本流入和流出来减少汇率的波动。 政府可以通过定向征税或条例颁布这项政策。

p217.original: Taxes on international capital flows are sometimes known as Tobin taxes, named after James Tobin, the 1981 Nobel laureate in economics who proposed such a tax in a 1972 lecture. For example, a government might tax all foreign exchange transactions, or attempt to tax short-term portfolio investment while exempting long-term foreign direct investment. Countries can also use regulation to forbid certain kinds of foreign investment in the first place or to make it difficult for international financial investors to withdraw their funds from a country.
p217.zh: 对国际资本流动的税收有时被称为托宾税,以1981年诺贝尔经济学奖得主詹姆斯·托宾的名字命名,他在1972年的一次讲座中提出了这样的税收. 例如,政府可能对所有外汇交易征税,或试图对短期证券投资征税,同时免除长期外国直接投资。 各国还可以利用监管来禁止某些种类的外国投资,或者使国际金融投资者难以从一个国家提取资金.

p218.original: The goal of such policies is to reduce international capital flows, especially short-term portfolio flows, in the hope that doing so will reduce the chance of large movements in exchange rates that can bring macroeconomic disaster.
p218.zh: 这些政策的目标是减少国际资本流动,特别是短期投资组合流动,希望这样做将减少汇率大变动的机会,从而带来宏观经济灾难。

p219.original: However, proposals to limit international financial flows have severe practical difficulties. National governments impose taxes, not international ones. If one government imposes a Tobin tax on exchange rate transactions carried out within its territory, a firm based someplace like the Grand Caymans, an island nation in the Caribbean well-known for allowing some financial wheeling and dealing might easily operate the exchange rate market. In an interconnected global economy, if goods and services are allowed to flow across national borders, then payments need to flow across borders, too. It is very difficult—in fact close to impossible—for a nation to allow only the flows of payments that relate to goods and services, while clamping down or taxing other flows of financial capital. If a nation participates in international trade, it must also participate in international capital movements.
p219.zh: 然而,限制国际资金流动的建议在实际中存在严重困难。国家政府实行税收,而不是国际税收。 如果一国政府对在其领土内进行的汇率交易征收托宾税,那么设在大开曼岛等地的公司,即加勒比一个因允许某些金融轮转和交易而闻名的岛屿国家,可能很容易经营汇率市场。 在相互关联的全球经济中,如果允许货物和服务跨界流动,那么付款也需要跨界流动。一个国家很难——事实上几乎不可能——只允许与货物和服务有关的付款流动,同时抑制或对其他金融资本流动征税。 如果一个国家参与国际贸易,它也必须参与国际资本流动。

p220.original: Finally, countries all over the world, especially low-income countries, are crying out for foreign investment to help develop their economies. Policies that discourage international financial investment may prevent some possible harm, but they rule out potentially substantial economic benefits as well.
p220.zh: 最后,世界各国,特别是低收入国家,都在呼吁外国投资帮助发展其经济。阻止国际金融投资的政策可以防止某些可能的伤害,但这种政策也排除了潜在的重大经济利益。

p221.original: A hard peg exchange rate policy will not allow short-term fluctuations in the exchange rate. If the government first announces a hard peg and then later changes its mind—perhaps the government becomes unwilling to keep interest rates high or to hold high levels of foreign exchange reserves—then the result of abandoning a hard peg could be a dramatic shift in the exchange rate.
p221.zh: 硬挂钩汇率政策将不允许汇率出现短期波动。 如果政府首先宣布硬挂钩,然后改变主意,也许政府不愿意保持高利率或保持高水平的外汇储备,那么放弃硬挂钩的结果可能是汇率的急剧变化。

p222.original: In the mid-2000s, about one-third of the countries in the world used a soft peg approach and about one-quarter used a hard peg approach. The general trend in the 1990s was to shift away from a soft peg approach in favor of either floating rates or a hard peg. The concern is that a successful soft peg policy may, for a time, lead to very little variation in exchange rates, so that firms and banks in the economy begin to act as if a hard peg exists. When the exchange rate does move, the effects are especially painful because firms and banks have not planned and hedged against a possible change. Thus, the argument went, it is better either to be clear that the exchange rate is always flexible, or that it is fixed, but choosing an in-between soft peg option may end up being worst of all.
p222.zh: 在2000年代中期,世界上约有三分之一的国家采用了软挂钩办法,大约四分之一的国家采用了硬挂钩办法。1990年代的总趋势是,从软挂钩办法转向浮动利率或硬挂钩。 人们担心的是,成功的软挂钩政策一段时间内可能导致汇率的极小变化,因此经济中的公司和银行开始像存在硬挂钩一样采取行动。 当汇率确实变动时,其影响尤其痛苦,因为公司和银行没有针对可能的变化进行计划和套期。 因此,这一论点认为,要么明确汇率总是灵活的,要么是固定的,但选择软挂钩方案之间的一种选择可能最糟糕。

p224.original: A final approach to exchange rate policy is for a nation to choose a common currency shared with one or more nations is also called a merged currency. A merged currency approach eliminates foreign exchange risk altogether. Just as no one worries about exchange rate movements when buying and selling between New York and California, Europeans know that the value of the euro will be the same in Germany and France and other European nations that have adopted the euro.
p224.zh: 汇率政策的最后一种做法是,一国选择与一个或多个国家共用的共同货币,也称为合并货币。合并的货币办法完全消除了外汇风险。 正如没有人担心纽约和加利福尼亚之间的汇率变动一样,欧洲人知道,在德国和法国以及采用欧元的其他欧洲国家,欧元的价值将是一样的。

p225.original: However, a merged currency also poses problems. Like a hard peg, a merged currency means that a nation has given up altogether on domestic monetary policy, and instead has put its interest rate policies in other hands. When Ecuador uses the U.S. dollar as its currency, it has no voice in whether the Federal Reserve raises or lowers interest rates. The European Central Bank that determines monetary policy for the euro has representatives from all the euro nations. However, from the standpoint of, say, Portugal, there will be times when the decisions of the European Central Bank about monetary policy do not match the decisions that a Portuguese central bank would have made.
p225.zh: 然而,合并货币也带来问题。与硬挂钩一样,合并货币意味着一个国家完全放弃国内货币政策,而将其利率政策交给其他方面。 当厄瓜多尔以美元为货币时,它对于美联储是否提高或降低利率没有发言权.确定欧元货币政策的欧洲中央银行有来自所有欧元国家的代表。 但是,从葡萄牙的角度来说,欧洲中央银行关于货币政策的决定有时与葡萄牙中央银行本来会作出的决定不符。

p226.original: The lines between these four different exchange rate policies can blend into each other. For example, a soft peg exchange rate policy in which the government almost never acts to intervene in the exchange rate market will look a great deal like a floating exchange rate. Conversely, a soft peg policy in which the government intervenes often to keep the exchange rate near a specific level will look a lot like a hard peg. A decision to merge currencies with another country is, in effect, a decision to have a permanently fixed exchange rate with those countries, which is like a very hard exchange rate peg.  summarizes the range of exchange rates policy choices, with their advantages and disadvantages.
p226.zh: 这四种不同的汇率政策之间的界线可以相互融合。 例如,软挂钩汇率政策,政府几乎从来不干预汇率市场,这种政策看起来将非常像浮动汇率。反之,软挂钩政策,政府经常介入,使汇率接近某一具体水平,这看起来将很像硬挂钩。与另一国合并货币的决定实际上是决定与这些国家实行永久性固定汇率,这就像一个非常硬的汇率挂钩。 该决定总结了汇率政策选择的范围及其利弊。

p233.original: Large short-run fluctuations in exchange rates?

p234.original: Often considerable in the short term

p235.original: Maybe less in the short run, but still large changes over time
p235.zh: 短期内可能还少,但随着时间的流逝,变化仍然很大

p236.original: None, unless a change in the fixed rate
p236.zh: 无,除非固定费率发生变化

p238.original: Large long-term fluctuations in exchange rates?

p241.original: Cannot happen unless hard peg changes, in which case substantial volatility can occur
p241.zh: 除非硬挂钩发生变化,否则不可能发生,在这种情况下,会发生巨大的波动

p243.original: Power of central bank to conduct countercyclical monetary policy?
p243.zh: 中央银行采取反周期货币政策的权力?

p244.original: Flexible exchange rates make monetary policy stronger
p244.zh: 灵活汇率使货币政策更加有力

p245.original: Some power, although conflicts may arise between exchange rate policy and countercyclical policy
p245.zh: 虽然汇率政策和反周期政策之间可能发生冲突,但有些权力

p246.original: Very little; central bank must keep exchange rate fixed
p246.zh: 很少;中央银行必须固定汇率

p247.original: None; nation does not have its own currency
p247.zh: 无;国家没有自己的货币

p248.original: Costs of holding foreign exchange reserves?

p249.original: Do not need to hold reserves

p250.original: Hold moderate reserves that rise and fall over time
p250.zh: 持有随时间推移而增减的中度储备

p253.original: Risk of ending up with an exchange rate that causes a large trade imbalance and very high inflows or outflows of financial capital?
p253.zh: 汇率导致大量贸易不平衡和金融资本流入或流出的风险?

p255.original: Adjusts over the medium term, if not the short term
p255.zh: 中期(如果不是短期)调整

p256.original: May end up over time either far above or below the market level
p256.zh: 最终可能远高于或低于市场水平

p258.original: Global macroeconomics would be easier if the whole world had one currency and one central bank. The exchange rates between different currencies complicate the picture. If financial markets solely set exchange rates, they fluctuate substantially as short-term portfolio investors try to anticipate tomorrow’s news. If the government attempts to intervene in exchange rate markets through soft pegs or hard pegs, it gives up at least some of the power to use monetary policy to focus on domestic inflations and recessions, and it risks causing even greater fluctuations in foreign exchange markets.
p258.zh: 如果全世界都有一个货币和一个中央银行,全球宏观经济就会更容易。不同货币之间的汇率使情况复杂化。 如果金融市场只设定汇率,那么随着短期证券投资者试图预测明天的消息,汇率波动很大。 如果政府试图通过软钉或硬钉干预汇率市场,它至少放弃了部分权力,可以使用货币政策来专注于国内通货膨胀和衰退,并有可能导致外汇市场更大的波动.

p259.original: There is no consensus among economists about which exchange rate policies are best: floating, soft peg, hard peg, or merged currencies. The choice depends both on how well a nation’s central bank can implement a specific exchange rate policy and on how well a nation’s firms and banks can adapt to different exchange rate policies. A national economy that does a fairly good job at achieving the four main economic goals of growth, low inflation, low unemployment, and a sustainable balance of trade will probably do just fine most of the time with any exchange rate policy. Conversely, no exchange rate policy is likely to save an economy that consistently fails at achieving these goals. Alternatively, a merged currency applied across wide geographic and cultural areas carries with it its own set of problems, such as the ability for countries to conduct their own independent monetary policies.
p259.zh: 经济学家对于哪些汇率政策是最好的没有共识:浮动、软挂钩、硬挂钩或合并货币。选择与否取决于一国中央银行能否执行具体的汇率政策,取决于一国企业和银行能否适应不同的汇率政策。一个国家经济在实现增长、低通胀、低失业率以及可持续的贸易平衡这四个主要经济目标方面做得相当好,很可能在大部分时间里都能够通过任何汇率政策来完善。 相反,任何汇率政策都不可能挽救一个一直未能实现这些目标的经济。 或者,在广泛的地理和文化领域采用合并货币,也伴随着其自身的问题,例如各国执行自己独立的货币政策的能力。

p260.original: Is a Stronger Dollar Good for the U.S. Economy?
p260.zh: 对美国来说是更强大的美元。经济?

p261.original: The foreign exchange value of the dollar is a price and whether a higher price is good or bad depends on where you are standing: sellers benefit from higher prices and buyers are harmed. A stronger dollar is good for U.S. imports (and people working for U.S. importers) and U.S. investment abroad. It is also good for U.S. tourists going to other countries, since their dollar goes further. However, a stronger dollar is bad for U.S. exports (and people working in U.S. export industries); it is bad for foreign investment in the United States (leading, for example, to higher U.S. interest rates); and it is bad for foreign tourists (as well as U.S hotels, restaurants, and others in the tourist industry). In short, whether the U.S. dollar is good or bad is a more complex question than you may have thought. The economic answer is “it depends.”
p261.zh: 美元外汇价值是一种价格,而高价是好还是坏取决于你所处的位置:卖方受益于高价,买方受到损害。更坚固的美元对美国进口(和为美国进口商工作的人)和美国海外投资都有好处. 这对前往其他国家的美国游客也有好处,因为他们的美元走得更远。 然而,更坚挺的美元对美国出口(以及在美国出口行业工作的人)来说是不好的;对美国的外国投资来说是不好的(例如导致美国利率的提高);对外国游客来说是不好的(还有美国酒店,餐馆,以及旅游业中的其他公司).简言之,美元是好是坏,是一个比你想的更复杂的问题.经济问题的答案是“这取决于” 。

p263.original: In a fixed exchange rate policy, a government determines its country’s exchange rate in the foreign exchange market. In a soft peg exchange rate policy, the foreign exchange market usually determines a country's exchange rate, but the government sometimes intervenes to strengthen or weaken it. In a hard peg exchange rate policy, the government chooses an exchange rate. A central bank can intervene in exchange markets in two ways. It can raise or lower interest rates to make the currency stronger or weaker. It also can directly purchase or sell its currency in foreign exchange markets. All exchange rates policies face tradeoffs. A hard peg exchange rate policy will reduce exchange rate fluctuations, but means that a country must focus its monetary policy on the exchange rate, not on fighting recession or controlling inflation. When a nation merges its currency with another nation, it gives up on nationally oriented monetary policy altogether.
p263.zh: 在固定汇率政策中,政府决定本国在外汇市场上的汇率。 在软挂钩汇率政策中,外汇市场通常决定一国的汇率,但政府有时会进行干预,加强或削弱汇率. 在硬挂钩汇率政策中,政府选择汇率.中央银行可以以两种方式干预外汇市场。它可以提高或降低利率,使货币更强或更弱. 它还可以在外汇市场上直接购买或出售其货币。 所有汇率政策都面临权衡。硬挂钩汇率政策将减少汇率波动,但意味着一国的货币政策必须侧重于汇率,而不是对抗衰退或控制通货膨胀。 当一个国家将其货币与另一个国家合并时,它完全放弃面向国家的货币政策。

p264.original: A soft peg exchange rate may create additional volatility as exchange rate markets try to anticipate when and how the government will intervene. A flexible exchange rate policy allows monetary policy to focus on inflation and unemployment, and allows the exchange rate to change with inflation and rates of return, but also raises a risk that exchange rates may sometimes make large and abrupt movements. The spectrum of exchange rate policies includes: (a) a floating exchange rate, (b) a pegged exchange rate, soft or hard, and (c) a merged currency. Monetary policy can focus on a variety of goals: (a) inflation; (b) inflation or unemployment, depending on which is the most dangerous obstacle; and (c) a long-term rule based policy designed to keep the money supply stable and predictable.
p264.zh: 由于汇率市场试图预测政府何时和如何进行干预,软挂钩汇率可能会造成更大的波动。灵活的汇率政策使货币政策能够侧重于通货膨胀和失业,并允许汇率随通货膨胀和回报率而变化,但也有可能使汇率有时发生巨大和突然的波动。汇率政策范围包括:(a) 浮动汇率,(b) 软或硬挂钩汇率,(c) 合并货币。货币政策可侧重于各种目标:(a) 通货膨胀;(b) 通货膨胀或失业,取决于哪些是最危险的障碍;(c) 基于规则的长期政策,旨在保持货币供应的稳定性和可预测性。

p266.original: How would a contractionary monetary policy affect the exchange rate, net exports, aggregate demand, and aggregate supply?
p266.zh: 收缩性货币政策如何影响汇率、净出口、总需求和总供应?

p267.original: A contractionary monetary policy, by driving up domestic interest rates, would cause the currency to appreciate. The higher value of the currency in foreign exchange markets would reduce exports, since from the perspective of foreign buyers, they are now more expensive. The higher value of the currency would similarly stimulate imports, since they would now be cheaper from the perspective of domestic buyers. Lower exports and higher imports cause net exports (EX – IM) to fall, which causes aggregate demand to fall. The result would be a decrease in GDP working through the exchange rate mechanism reinforcing the effect contractionary monetary policy has on domestic investment expenditure. However, cheaper imports would stimulate aggregate supply, bringing GDP back to potential, though at a lower price level.
p267.zh: 紧缩的货币政策,通过推动国内利率上升,将使货币升值。外汇市场上货币价值的提高将减少出口,因为从外国买家的角度来看,现在这些货币更加昂贵。货币的较高价值同样会刺激进口,因为从国内买家的角度来看,现在这种价格会更便宜。出口下降和进口增加导致净出口(EX – IM)下降,导致总需求下降。其结果是,通过汇率机制减少国内生产总值,强化收缩性货币政策对国内投资支出的影响。 然而,较便宜的进口品将刺激总供应,使国内生产总值恢复潜力,尽管价格水平较低。

p268.original: A central bank can allow its currency to fall indefinitely, but it cannot allow its currency to rise indefinitely. Why not?
p268.zh: 中央银行可以允许其货币无限期下跌,但不能允许其货币无限期上升. 为什么不呢?

p269.original: For a currency to fall, a central bank need only supply more of its currency in foreign exchange markets. It can print as much domestic currency as it likes. For a currency to rise, a central bank needs to buy its currency in foreign exchange markets, paying with foreign currency. Since no central bank has an infinite amount of foreign currency reserves, it cannot buy its currency indefinitely.
p269.zh: 要让货币贬值,中央银行只需要在外汇市场上提供更多的货币。它可以印出像它喜欢的一样多的国内货币.货币要上升,中央银行需要在外汇市场上购买其货币,用外币支付. 由于任何中央银行都没有无限的外汇储备,因此不能无限期地购买其货币.

p270.original: Is a country for which imports and exports comprise a large fraction of the GDP more likely to adopt a flexible exchange rate or a fixed (hard peg) exchange rate?
p270.zh: 对于一个进出口占国内生产总值很大一部分的国家来说,采用灵活汇率或固定(硬挂钩)汇率的可能性更大吗?

p271.original: Variations in exchange rates, because they change import and export prices, disturb international trade flows. When trade is a large part of a nation’s economic activity, government will find it more advantageous to fix exchange rates to minimize disruptions of trade flows.
p271.zh: 汇率的变动,因为它们改变了进出口价格,扰乱了国际贸易流动。 当贸易是国家经济活动的一大部分时,政府会发现确定汇率以尽量减少贸易流动的中断更为有利。

p273.original: What is the difference between a floating exchange rate, a soft peg, a hard peg, and dollarization?
p273.zh: 浮动汇率,软挂钩,硬挂钩,硬挂钩与美元化有何区别?

p274.original: List some advantages and disadvantages of the different exchange rate policies.
p274.zh: 列出不同汇率政策的一些利弊.

p276.original: Many developing countries, like Mexico, have moderate to high rates of inflation. At the same time, international trade plays an important role in their economies. What type of exchange rate regime would be best for such a country’s currency vis à vis the U.S. dollar?
p276.zh: 许多发展中国家,如墨西哥,通货膨胀率中高。 与此同时,国际贸易在它们的经济中发挥着重要作用。什么样的汇率制度最适合这种国家的货币对美元的汇率?

p277.original: What would make a country decide to change from a common currency, like the euro, back to its own currency?
p277.zh: 是什么使一个国家决定从共同货币,如欧元,回到自己的货币?

p279.original: Friedman, Milton. Capitalism and Freedom. Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 1962.
p279.zh: (原始内容存档于2018-09-29). Friedman, Milton.资本主义与自由.芝加哥:芝加哥大学出版社,1962年.

c0.original: Is a trade deficit between the United States and the European Union good or bad for the U.S. economy? (Credit: modification of “US Dollar banknotes” by Milad Mosapoor/Wikimedia Commons, Public Domain)
c0.zh: 美国和欧洲联盟之间的贸易逆差对美国经济有利还是不利?(编辑:Milad Mosapoor/Wikimedia Communications,公共领域对“美元钞票”的修改)

c1.original: The “% Daily Share” shows the percentage of transactions where the currency is on one side of the exchange. (Source: https://www.bis.org/statistics/rpfx19_fx.pdf)
c1.zh: “每日份额百分比”显示货币在交易所一方的交易百分比。(资料来源:https://www.bis.org/statistics/rpfx19_fx.pdf).

c2.original: Expectations of a currency's future value can drive its demand and supply in foreign exchange markets.
c2.zh: 对货币未来价值的预期可以推动其在外汇市场上的供求。

c3.original: Exchange rates tend to fluctuate substantially, even between bordering companies such as the United States and Canada.  By looking closely at the time values, it is clear that the values in part (a) are a mirror image of part (b), which demonstrates that the depreciation of one currency correlates to the appreciation of the other and vice versa.  This means that when comparing the exchange rates between two countries (in this case, the United States and Canada), the depreciation (or weakening) of one country (the U.S. dollar for this example) indicates the appreciation (or strengthening) of the other currency (which in this example is the Canadian dollar). (Source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) https://research.stlouisfed.org/fred2/series/EXCAUS)
c3.zh: 汇率往往波动很大,甚至在美国和加拿大等毗邻公司之间也是如此。 通过仔细观察时间值,显然(a)部分的值是(b)部分的镜像,这表明一种货币的贬值与另一种货币的升值有关,反之亦然。 这意味着在比较两个国家(此处为美国和加拿大)的汇率时,一个国家(以美元为例)的贬值(或疲软)表明另一种货币(此处为加拿大元)的升值(或升值).(资料来源:联邦储备经济数据(FRED) https://research.stlouisfed.org/fred2/series/EXCAUS).

c4.original: Exchange rate movements affect exporters, tourists, and international investors in different ways.
c4.zh: 汇率波动以不同方式影响出口商、游客和国际投资者。

c5.original: (a) The quantity measured on the horizontal axis is in U.S. dollars, and the exchange rate on the vertical axis is the price of U.S. dollars measured in Mexican pesos. (b) The quantity measured on the horizontal axis is in Mexican pesos, while the price on the vertical axis is the price of pesos measured in U.S. dollars. In both graphs, the equilibrium exchange rate occurs at point E, at the intersection of the demand curve (D) and the supply curve (S).
c5.zh: (a) 水平轴上测得的数量以美元计,垂直轴上的汇率以墨西哥比索计价。(b) 水平轴上测得的量用墨西哥比索计,而垂直轴上测得的价格则用美元计得的量用比索计。 在这两个图中,均衡汇率发生在E点,需求曲线(D)和供应曲线(S)的交汇处.

c6.original: An announcement that the peso exchange rate is likely to strengthen in the future will lead to greater demand for the peso in the present from investors who wish to benefit from the appreciation. Similarly, it will make investors less likely to supply pesos to the foreign exchange market. Both the shift of demand to the right and the shift of supply to the left cause an immediate appreciation in the exchange rate.
c6.zh: 宣布比索汇率今后可能提高,将导致希望从升值中获益的投资者对比索的更大需求。 同样,这将减少投资者向外汇市场供应比索的可能性。需求向右转移和供应向左转移,都造成汇率立即升值。

c7.original: A higher rate of return for U.S. dollars makes holding dollars more attractive. Thus, the demand for dollars in the foreign exchange market shifts to the right, from D0 to D1, while the supply of dollars shifts to the left, from S0 to S1. The new equilibrium (E1) has a stronger exchange rate than the original equilibrium (E0), but in this example, the equilibrium quantity traded does not change.
c7.zh: 较高的美元收益率使得持有美元更具吸引力. 因此,外汇市场对美元的需求从D0转向D1,而美元的供应则从S0转向S1。新的平衡(E1)的汇率比原来的平衡(E0)要强,但在这个例子中,交易的平衡数量并没有变化.

c8.original: If a currency is experiencing relatively high inflation, then its buying power is decreasing and international investors will be less eager to hold it. Thus, a rise in inflation in the Mexican peso would lead demand to shift from D0 to D1, and supply to increase from S0 to S1. Both movements in demand and supply would cause the currency to depreciate. Here, we draw no effect on the quantity traded, but in truth it could be an increase or a decrease, depending on the actual movements of demand and supply.
c8.zh: 如果某一货币正经历相对较高的通货膨胀,那么其购买力正在下降,国际投资者将不太渴望持有该货币。 因此,墨西哥比索通货膨胀的上升将导致需求从D0转向D1,供应从S0增加到S1。供需两方面的变动都会导致货币贬值。 在这方面,我们对交易的数量没有任何影响,但事实上,这可以是增加或减少,这取决于需求和供应的实际流动情况。

c9.original: The scenario of international borrowing that ends on the left is a success story, but the scenario that ends on the right shows what happens when the exchange rate weakens.
c9.zh: 以左为结束的国际借款的情景是一个成功的故事,但以右为结束的情景显示了汇率减弱时会发生什么.

c10.original: A nation may adopt one of a variety of exchange rate regimes, from floating rates in which the foreign exchange market determines the rates to pegged rates where governments intervene to manage the exchange rate's value, to a common currency where the nation adopts another country or group of countries' currency.
c10.zh: 一个国家可以采用各种汇率制度之一,从外汇市场决定汇率的浮动汇率到政府干预管理汇率价值的挂钩汇率,到国家采用另一国或国家集团货币的共同货币。

c11.original: Even seemingly stable exchange rates such as the Japanese Yen to the U.S. Dollar can vary when closely examined over time. This figure shows a relatively stable rate between 2000 and 2007 of over 25%. Beginning in 2007 until 2012, there was a significant appreciation of the Yen (relative to the U.S. Dollar) by about 14% and again at the end of the year in 2014 also by about 14%. Since then, between 2016 and 2020 there was an appreciation of about 13% from 118 yen per dollar to 103 yen per dollar. (Source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) https://research.stlouisfed.org/fred2/series/DEXJPUS)
c11.zh: 即使是日本对美日元等看似稳定的汇率.美元随时间推移而变化。这一数字显示,2000年至2007年期间,相对稳定的比率超过25%。 从2007年开始直到2012年,对"日元"(相对于美国)给予了显著的赏识.(美元)约14%,2014年年末再次增加14%左右。 此后,2016年至2020年间,从118日元兑1美元到103日元兑1美元升值约13%.(资料来源:联邦储备经济数据(FRED) https://research.stlouisfed.org/fred2/series/DEXJPUS) 互联网档案馆的存檔,存档日期2013-09-02.

c12.original: (a) If an exchange rate is pegged below what would otherwise be the equilibrium, then the currency's quantity demanded will exceed the quantity supplied. (b) If an exchange rate is pegged above what would otherwise be the equilibrium, then the currency's quantity supplied exceeds the quantity demanded.
c12.zh: (a) 如果某一汇率低于原为平衡的汇率,则所要求货币的数量将超过所供应的数量。(b) 如果某一汇率与原本的平衡水平相挂钩,则该货币的供应量将超过所要求的数量。
